channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Real And Wild — RAW Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Inaugural edition of RAW, a nature photography award built around a single rule: every image must be made within 100 km of the photographer's home — 'the wild is not far away.' Five categories: RAW Neighbors (no human elements), Coexistence (human presence), Connection (people and nature), Macro (the small world) and Perspective (the big scene). The Real And Wild Photographer of the Year receives $1,000, with $250 for each category winner; winning and shortlisted images are published in the online RAW Winners Gallery and a photo book, and promoted through a partnership with Atlantic Geographic. Blind judging by professionals. Open worldwide, with a free RAW Junior tier for under-18s. Fees: $10 for one image, $25 for five, $40 for ten. AI-generated or AI-composited images are not permitted. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $10–$40. Prize: $1,000 grand prize + $250 per category + Photobook.

item.title: AOP Emerging Talent Award 2026 · Association of Photographers
item.description: AOP Project Award celebrating the new wave of photographers and image-makers who have been practicing professionally — full or part-time — for under three years. No subject restrictions: enter in three formats — Stills (a single image or a 2–5 image series), Moving Image (up to 7 minutes), or Innovation (creative use of AR, VR, CGI or other techniques). Open to AOP members and non-members alike, of any age or background. Judged by established professionals and industry representatives. The Gold winner receives a tailored AOP Associate Membership package built around their career path: 1:1 folio reviews with industry representatives, an AOP Business Practice Review worth £500, and a 12-month professional mentorship — plus a BUILDHOLLYWOOD digital billboard display across London worth £8,520. Gold and Silver winners and selected finalists are exhibited in late 2026 and featured in an Awards publication. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: £10 / £15 single (member / non-member). Prize: AOP membership + London billboard + Exhibition.

item.title: Night Vision · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at Artlink Contemporary Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana celebrating those who are drawn to the vivid colors of the dark and the possibilities of the night. Open to artists working in all media — painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, ceramic, video, installation, collage, printmaking, jewelry, mixed media, and beyond. Up to 10 work samples; open to US artists 18 and over. Exhibition runs September 3–27, 2026 at Artlink in Fort Wayne. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: $12 + $12 media fee. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Standing Where Others Stood — Summer 2026 Online Exhibition · Analog Forever Magazine
item.description: Analog Forever Magazine's Summer 2026 online group exhibition, guest-curated by Dana Stirling and Yoav Friedlander of Float Photo Magazine. The brief turns to the outdoors — photographs that capture the sense of wonder, curiosity, nostalgia, and discovery that accompanies time spent in the landscape, and the feeling of standing where others have stood before. This is an analog/film exhibition: every submitted work must include at least one analog component, and fully digital photographs and AI-generated images are not eligible. One image per artist, submitted free through a Google Form. Selected work is shown in an online group exhibition that launches August 28, 2026. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Legacy · Ajanaku Gallery
item.description: Founding exhibition of Ajanaku Gallery — a photo-and-text show exploring Afro-Caribbean heritage, transmission, and memory, built on the idea of 'what our ancestors left us, and what we will leave to the world.' Open internationally to photographers, writers, and poets: works pair images (portraits, symbolic scenes, ritual objects, revisited traditional garments) with integrated texts such as original poems, African and Caribbean proverbs, letter fragments, and meditative writing. Free to enter through the gallery's online form; submit up to two works as high-resolution JPG, PNG, or PDF (max 10MB each, no zip files). Selected artists become part of the gallery's founding narrative, with their work shown in the exhibition and an accompanying publication. The exhibition runs 16–23 December 2026 in Neuilly-Plaisance, France. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: The City Series: London — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
item.description: Open call for The City Series: London, the next volume in Shutter Hub Editions’ ongoing series of photobooks exploring the people, places, and cultures that shape cities worldwide. Rather than documenting a location as a fixed subject, the series invites photographers to respond to a city as an idea — something experienced, observed, imagined, and interpreted through the photographic eye. Selected images are featured in a printed 100-image photobook, sold through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists, with a launch event in London on 20 November 2026. Pay-what-you-can entry with a £15 minimum; free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide, up to 10 images per submission. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: £15+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Festival di Fotografia a Capri 2026 — Viaggi e Miraggi
item.description: Open call for the 18th edition of the Festival di Fotografia a Capri, organised by Fondazione Capri, on the theme 'Viaggi e Miraggi' (Travels and Mirages) — inspired by the 200th anniversary of the rediscovery of the Blue Grotto and exploring real and imagined journeys. Open worldwide to photographers, amateurs and professionals, free of charge. Submit a project as a single PDF in a .zip folder (max 10MB) by email to festival@fondazionecapri.org, with the images, a short descriptive text, and a biography. A jury formed by the Directorate of Museums and Archaeological Parks of Capri and Fondazione Capri selects the winning project, exhibited at the Chiostro della Certosa di San Giacomo during the festival, 30 August – 11 October 2026. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at the Certosa.

item.title: Gaze – The Queer Photo Award 2026
item.description: Annual queer photo award created by and for the LGBTQIA+ community, hosted in Germany by Brendel, Vogel & Weber GbR (agency Vielformat) with camera reseller MPB as sponsor. The 2026 theme, 'HOW TO / GATHER – Queer Communities in Photography', seeks work exploring queer spaces, forms of community, care and chosen families — relationships beyond heteronormative-patriarchal norms, and what happens when queer spaces are under threat. Open to LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists aged 18+ resident in Germany, the EU or the UK. Submit a project of 1–5 photographs or a series of up to 5 images, taken within the last five years. A National and an International first prize of €1,000 each (MPB vouchers) plus a €500 Audience Prize are awarded; winning entries are shown in an exhibition in Berlin in winter 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: 2× €1,000 + €500 + Berlin exhibition.

item.title: Are Men OK? · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Open call from Fotografiska Emerging and Fotografiska Stockholm, in partnership with the men's-issues organisation MÄN and timed to Men's Health Week, inviting emerging photographers and visual artists to explore what it means to be a man in Sweden today. Submissions may address identity, belonging, loneliness, friendship, care, vulnerability, strength, community, tradition or change — through personal stories, documentary perspectives, staged images, intimate observations or broader social reflections, with a particular welcome for voices and experiences rarely given space. Selected works will be presented in a group exhibition at Fotografiska Stockholm in autumn 2026. Curated by Fotografiska's Johan Vikner and Sofia Liljergren. Free to enter. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fotografiska Stockholm exhibition.

item.title: The Curated Fridge — Summer 2026 Show
item.description: Seasonal juried photography show from The Curated Fridge, the long-running Somerville project that exhibits selected prints on its now-iconic refrigerator and shares the work online. The Summer 2026 open call has no theme and is juried by Rachel Vogel, Assistant Curator at the Addison Gallery of American Art. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional; submit up to 5 images. Selected work is shown in the physical Fridge Show and posted on the TCF website and social media. Entry is free, but participants must both email JPEGs and mail printed photographs (no larger than 4x6 or 5x5 inches) to the Somerville address. No AI photography. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Online feature.

item.title: Creatures · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe celebrating animals in their element — wild, domestic, aquatic, and everything in between, across all habitats and settings. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, who selects 26 images for the gallery walls. The gallery covers professional Luster-paper printing, matting, and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px on the longest side). Exhibition October 2–30, 2026 with an opening reception; post-exhibition sales split 50/50. $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Through The Lens 2026 · Yeiser Art Center
item.description: The Yeiser Art Center's long-running annual international juried photography exhibition, held in the historic 1905 Market House building in downtown Paducah, Kentucky. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over working in photo-based imagery created through photographic processes — including non-lens-made images — completed within the last three years. A juror selects 50–70 images for the gallery exhibition. $1,000 in cash awards: First Place $500, Second Place $300, Third Place $200. Up to 20 images may be entered at $10 each (Yeiser members receive $10 off). Exhibition August 25 – October 11, 2026; the gallery takes a 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: $10/image. Prize: $1,000 in cash + Exhibition.

item.title: Eurazeo Photo Prize 2026
item.description: Eurazeo, a leading European private asset manager, relaunches its long-running photography patronage as the Eurazeo Photo Prize — now a project-development grant anchored in the company's Endowment Fund. Open to professional photographers of all nationalities, based in France or abroad, it invites applicants to submit a project for development. Each year one laureate receives a €20,000 grant to deliver an ambitious long-term body of work, plus dedicated artistic and strategic guidance and connections with galleries, festivals, media and leading industry professionals. Building on the Eurazeo Photo Prize that ran annually from 2010 to 2025, the new grant supports creation earlier in the process. Marking the bicentenary of photography, applications are open 2 June – 13 September 2026; free to enter. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €20,000.

item.title: Landscape 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of landscape — the power of landscape photography to inspire awe and transport viewers to places they may never experience in person. Selected work is shown in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–28 November 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants are put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Prints are produced on photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Stories 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of stories — photographs that tell powerful narratives about people, places, and events, with documentary, reportage, and street photography as its strongest tools. Selected work is shown in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (4–28 November 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants are put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Prints are produced on photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Guest Room: Sunyoung Kim & Shinwook Kim · Der Greif
item.description: Open call curated by Sunyoung Kim (Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum) and artist Shinwook Kim, on the theme "Hyperobjects: Archipelagic Memories" — exploring how photographs circulate across digital and material networks, fragmenting and reshaping personal and collective histories. Selected work is featured on Der Greif's platform, and selected artists receive a face-to-face feedback session with the curators. One artist receives a €250 Guest Room scholarship. Open globally; works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible. — Deadline: July 13, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: €250 scholarship.

item.title: Preus Museum Open Call 2026 — Passion
item.description: Annual themed open call from Preus Museum, the National Museum of Photography in Norway, presented with the Oslo Negativ photo festival. The 2026 theme is "Passion." Open to all artists worldwide, professional or amateur, individually or as a collective. Submit single images or a series of up to 15 photographs exploring the theme, with a project description explaining how the work relates to it. One winner receives NOK 20,000, acquisition into the Preus Museum collection, and an exhibition at Oslo Negativ 2026, with production and travel costs covered by the museum. Entry fee €10; free for students and Norwegian photographers via voucher (email opencall@preusmuseum.no). — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: NOK 20,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: The EcoTheo Review — 2026 Visual Art Call
item.description: Open call for visual art — including photography — for The EcoTheo Review, the quarterly print magazine of EcoTheo Collective, a 501(c)3 nonprofit that celebrates wonder and explores the intersection of ecology, spirituality, and art across all traditions. Work is reviewed on a rolling basis; selected pieces run across the four annual print issues plus the website and social channels, sometimes paired with essays, statements, or interviews. International, open to all forms of original visual art suitable for high-quality print reproduction. Submit 1–10 works for a $10 fee. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: Print publication.

item.title: FLOAT Magazine — Let's Get the F@!#k Outta Here
item.description: Themed open call for FLOAT Photo Magazine's upcoming print issue, inviting lens-based work that engages with humanity's growing fascination with looking beyond Earth — Mars, UFOs, space travel, extraterrestrial life, and the urge for escape. FLOAT is an independent photography magazine that welcomes all photographic styles and looks for cohesive, thought-out bodies of work. Selected photographers are published in the printed issue and receive a complimentary contributor copy (the artist covers shipping); additional copies are sold online and at book fairs, and photographers retain full copyright. Submit 1–10 images for a $9 entry fee via the magazine's store and a linked form. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $9 (1–10 images). Prize: Print publication + Contributor copy.

item.title: Abundance — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by independent curator Lauren Hirshfield, opening September 4, 2026. The theme invites artists to consider cycles of care, giving, and receiving — what abundance looks like, and how it might be manifested. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after August 3, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: Macadam Awards 2026 · Street Macadam
item.description: Third edition of the Macadam Awards, a street and documentary photography contest from the Street Macadam collective. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers aged 18 and over, on any street or documentary subject. The three winners and twenty honorable mentions are published in EPIC magazine (December 2026) and featured on All About Photo, and winning images are exhibited at two festivals — the Rome Photo Festival (October 2026) and the MX Street Photo Fest in Querétaro, Mexico (October–November 2026). Judged by an international jury spanning thirteen nationalities. First prize is a Ricoh GR III Street Edition camera plus a WANDRD PRVKE backpack; second and third place receive camera slings. Entry is €8 for a single photo up to €35 for ten. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: €8–€35. Prize: Ricoh GR III camera + Exhibitions + Publication.

item.title: Life Framer — Humans
item.description: Monthly photography competition judged by documentary photographer GMB Akash. Theme: the people of the world, from individuals to crowds — portraiture, studio, candid, conceptual, travel, street, composite, and environmental work, exploring identity in all its forms. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Grand Prix de la Photographie Paris Match 2026
item.description: For the Bicentenary of Photography, Paris Match launches its first national photography Grand Prix on the theme 'Un regard sur notre époque' (A Look at Our Time). Open to everyone across France, amateurs and enthusiasts alike, it invites photographers to capture contemporary France in all its diversity and contradictions. Entrants submit a series of four original photographs across thematic categories — among them creativity, daring, family and transmission, each backed by a partner (Google France, Bpifrance, VistaPrint, CCF | KOREGE). A jury selects the finalists, revealed in autumn 2026, with an exhibition and awards ceremony on 16 December 2026. Each grand-public category winner receives a prize from Paris Match and its partners plus featured visibility to the magazine's readers. Submissions run 11 June – 19 July 2026. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Paris Match feature.

item.title: Mobile Photography Awards 2026
item.description: The 15th annual Mobile Photography Awards (MPA), the longest-running international competition dedicated to photographs shot and edited entirely on mobile phones and tablets. Twelve photo categories plus a dedicated Photo Essay category; each image may be entered in up to two categories. Over $10,000 in total prizes including a $3,000 Grand Prize, $250 per category winner and a $500 Photo Essay prize, with winners exhibited. Open worldwide to anyone shooting on a mobile device. Tiered entry fees from $15 for a single image up to $149 for 25 images ($29 for the Photo Essay category). Entries run through December 18, 2026. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: $15–$149. Prize: $3,000 grand prize + $10,000 pool.

item.title: World Nature Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The seventh edition of the World Nature Photography Awards (WNPA), an international nature and wildlife photography competition. Fourteen categories spanning Animals in their habitat, Animal portraits, behaviour categories (Bird, Mammal, Amphibian/Reptile, Invertebrate), Plants and fungi, Urban wildlife, Landscapes, Underwater, Black and white, Nature art, Photojournalism and People and nature. Gold, silver and bronze winners in every category; the top-scoring gold image wins the World Nature Photographer of the Year title plus $1,000. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide aged 18+; images of captive or restrained animals are not permitted. Standard entry is £30 for up to six images, with no limit on the number of entries. Submissions accepted online only as JPEGs (1,000–3,000px, under 3MB). Deadline midnight GMT, 30 June 2026. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: £30. Prize: $1,000 + Photographer of the Year.

item.title: Sony World Photography Awards 2027
item.description: One of the world's leading photography awards, run by the World Photography Organisation and free to enter since its inception. Four competitions: the Series competition (5–10 image projects across ten categories) where the overall Photographer of the Year wins $25,000, a solo presentation at the London exhibition and Sony Digital Imaging equipment; the Single Image competition (up to three single images free) with a $5,000 overall prize; plus dedicated Student (photography students worldwide) and Youth (under-19) competitions. Category winners and shortlisted photographers receive global press exposure, inclusion in the awards book and exhibition. Single Image closes 5 January 2027; Series closes 12 January 2027 (16:00 GMT). Shortlist and winners announced spring 2027, exhibition at Somerset House, London. — Deadline: January 12, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $25,000 + solo exhibition + Sony gear.

item.title: Nature and Humans Photo Competition 2026 · DESEA Foundation
item.description: Fourth edition of the DESEA Foundation's international nature and conservation photography competition (Madrid, Spain). Fifteen awarded categories: four conservation photojournalism categories (Series, Single Image, Spain, and 'Conservation Told by Women'), two WildWatchingSpain special categories, six thematic categories (Mammals, Birds, Oceans, Other Animals, Landscape, Creative), plus Young, Child and People's Choice awards. Around €17,000 in total prizes including cash awards plus camera gear from Sony and OM System. Open to amateur and professional photographers of any nationality; up to 30 images, JPG minimum 3000px on the longest side. FONAMAD members pay €15; under-18s enter free. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: €25 (free under-18). Prize: €17,000 prize pool.

item.title: pARTy 'til the Cows Come Home · The Firefly Artists
item.description: 5th annual juried exhibition from Long Island artist cooperative The Firefly Artists heralding Northport's Great Cow Harbor Day Weekend — a "moo-ving" celebration of cows, farm life, the Cow Harbor 10K race weekend, and the Village of Northport itself. Street photography of Cow Harbor Weekend is particularly appreciated, and all original 2D and 3D media up to 36"×36" are accepted, photography included. First through third place and honorable mention awards; exhibition at the gallery at 90 Main Street August 26 – September 27, 2026, with reception September 17 during race week. All work for sale, 35% commission. — Deadline: August 5, 2026. Fee: $35 (+$5 each addl). Prize: Gallery exhibition + 1st-3rd place awards.

item.title: Inspired by Cape Cod · Cape Cod Art Center
item.description: Summer online all-media exhibit from Cape Cod Art Center inviting photographers and studio artists to submit work inspired by Cape Cod — its light, landscapes, and life. Up to 5 entries per artist at $15 per piece, with a maximum of 2 works accepted. Cash awards for Best of Show/First Place, Second Place, and Honorable Mention. The online exhibition goes live August 10, 2026. — Deadline: July 26, 2026. Fee: $15/piece. Prize: Cash awards + Online exhibition.

item.title: Landscapes for Landsake 2026 · Agricultural Stewardship Association
item.description: 25th annual juried art sale and exhibition benefiting the Agricultural Stewardship Association, a land trust conserving farmland and forests in New York's Washington and Rensselaer counties. Work in 2D and 3D media — photography and print included — should draw inspiration from the agricultural landscapes, products, people, and rural life of the Taconic and Upper Hudson regions, traditional or interpretive. Around 300 works hang in the historic barn at Maple Ridge in Cambridge, NY, October 9–11, 2026, with an online exhibition continuing through November 15. Free to enter; participating artists donate 50% of proceeds to ASA's conservation work. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Kenmore Art Show 2026: Togetherness
item.description: Annual community juried show at Kenmore City Hall north of Seattle, themed 'Togetherness' for 2026 and inviting artists across the Pacific Northwest. Photography (film or digital) is one of four categories alongside 2D, 3D and the Little Gallery of small works. Per-category awards of $200/$150/$100 plus $300 Best in Show, $200 People's Choice and a Mayor's Purchase Award. Up to 2 pieces per category, hand-delivered; exhibition August 14–23, 2026. — Deadline: June 26, 2026. Fee: $25 ($15 2nd piece). Prize: $300 Best in Show + category awards.

item.title: Works on Paper · The Firefly Artists
item.description: National juried works-on-paper exhibition from Long Island artist cooperative The Firefly Artists, hung at the Darcy Arts Center in Northport, NY, July 21 – August 21, 2026. Photography is explicitly accepted alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, mixed media and digital media — original, human-made 2D works on paper up to 36"×36". First through third place and honorable mention awards; all work for sale with a 35% gallery commission. Reception August 6. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: $35 (+$5 each addl). Prize: Gallery exhibition + 1st-3rd place awards.

item.title: Peggy Doole National Small Works 2026 · Washington Print Foundation
item.description: 28th annual national small-works competition honoring printmaking advocate Peggy Doole, exhibited at Washington Printmakers Gallery in Washington, DC, July 30 – August 30, 2026. Accepts hand-pulled prints, screen prints, digital prints, fine art photographs and 3D work with print components — 2D work up to 250 square inches framed, made within the past two years. Juried by Washington art critic Mark Jenkins. $1,000 Grand Prize and $750 Washington Print Foundation Prize; reception August 1. — Deadline: July 3, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000 Grand Prize + $750 WPF Prize.

item.title: 97th Michigan Contemporary Art Exhibition · Muskegon Museum of Art
item.description: 97th edition of the Muskegon Museum of Art's statewide juried exhibition, on view September 10 – November 4, 2026. Open to Michigan artists 18+ working in any medium except video and performance; photography and digital prints should be from limited editions. Up to two original works completed in the last two years. Juried by Detroit-born photographer Lauren Semivan (MFA, Cranbrook Academy of Art). Best of Show $1,500, second place $1,000, third place $750, plus additional prizes. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $35 ($20 members). Prize: $1,500 + $1,000 + $750.

item.title: The Beauty of It · Old Town Arts & Crafts Guild
item.description: 8th annual juried competition from the Old Town Arts & Crafts Guild, a community gallery on Long Island's North Fork founded in 1948. Entries in three categories — Fine Art, Photography, and Mixed Media/Crafts — with $150/$100/$75 awards in each. Juried by artist Esther Marie Caponigro. Accepted work is exhibited and offered for sale in the Guild's virtual exhibition August 1 – September 30, 2026 (30% commission on sales). — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (+$5 each addl). Prize: $150/$100/$75 per category.

item.title: Leigh Weimers Emerging Artists Awards 2026 · Rotary Club of San Jose
item.description: Annual unrestricted cash awards from the Rotary Club of San Jose honoring Mercury News columnist Leigh Weimers, for emerging artists whose work meaningfully engages or benefits residents of Santa Clara County (county residency itself not required). Visual arts including photography, plus music, literary and performance categories. Up to four winners receive grants that have ranged from $1,000 to $5,000 and present their work at the SJSU Hammer Theatre Center on October 21. Applicants should show some professional achievement but not yet wide recognition. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: Up to 4 grants of $1,000-$5,000.

item.title: Open Call: All Media 2026 · Studio Channel Islands
item.description: International juried exhibition in Studio Channel Islands' 3,000-square-foot gallery in Camarillo, California, August 1 – September 12, 2026. All media and styles welcome — including photography — for 2D/3D, video, film, performance, sound and installation work completed in the last three years; the prospectus asks for 'breakthrough pieces' that mark a turning point in your practice. Juried by Patricia Sweetow of Patricia Sweetow Gallery (Los Angeles). Cash prizes of $1,000/$750/$500 plus three juror's awards; 60/40 split on sales. — Deadline: July 7, 2026. Fee: $55 ($35 members). Prize: $1,000 + $750 + $500.

item.title: Kometa Fellows Program 2026
item.description: Fellowship from Kometa, the French magazine of on-the-ground reporting from zones of war, censorship, and political tension. Up to six fellows each receive €10,000 to complete a field-based project within one year, with monthly editorial support and an exclusivity agreement with the magazine. Open internationally to documentary photographers, photojournalists, journalists, and writers; this first 2026 call focuses on disinformation and narrative wars, and political and social change in the Gulf. Projects already under contract with a publisher are not eligible. A second call follows in winter 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €10,000 grant.

item.title: Betty Bowen Award 2026 · Seattle Art Museum
item.description: 49th annual Betty Bowen Award from the Seattle Art Museum for visual artists living and working in Washington, Oregon, or Idaho. The winner receives a $20,000 unrestricted cash prize and a solo exhibition at SAM; up to two Special Recognition Awards of $4,000 and three Special Commendation Awards of $2,500 are also given, and all finalists receive a $500 honorarium. First-round review by the Betty Bowen Committee is anonymous. All media accepted, including photography. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $20,000 + Solo exhibition at SAM.

item.title: Echoes: Revisiting Memory · Crooked Tree Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Crooked Tree Arts Center's Gilbert Gallery in Petoskey, Michigan, on memory engaged literally and metaphorically, juried by Paige Young, Assistant Professor of Photography at Kendall College of Art and Design. Open to artists 18+ in the Great Lakes region (Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Ontario). Cash awards of $500, $300, and $200; works must be from the past three years. Exhibition September 18 – October 31, 2026. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: $30 ($20 members). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: Series: One Thing After Another · Site:Brooklyn Gallery
item.description: Online juried exhibition from Site:Brooklyn Gallery on contemporary seriality — how artists use series, repetition, and sequential approaches across all media. Juried by Matt Stromberg, freelance arts writer and educator contributing to Hyperallergic and the Los Angeles Times. Open internationally to artists 18+; all work must be for sale with a 60% artist commission. Exhibition online August 21 – September 21, 2026. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: $26 + $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Kinhouse: Exploring Kinship and the Spaces We Inhabit
item.description: National juried exhibition at Kinhouse Gallery & Residency in Fort Wayne, Indiana, seeking work on belonging, grounding, connection, and rootedness — with particular interest in the domestic sphere, caregiving, heritage, place, legacy, and community. Juried by Braydee Euliss, Indianapolis-based curator and founder of COMPANION gallery. Selected artists receive a $25 shipping stipend and possible inclusion in an extended exhibition catalog. Exhibition August 21 – September 30, 2026. — Deadline: June 28, 2026. Fee: $22. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog publication.

item.title: Transformation · Art Works Downtown
item.description: Juried exhibition at Art Works Downtown's 1337 Gallery in San Rafael, California, on the theme of transformation, juried by PJ Gubatina Policarpio, Curator at Root Division. Open to San Francisco Bay Area artists living within 100 miles of San Rafael; all visual media accepted, including photography. No giclées or reproductions. Exhibition August 7 – September 18, 2026. — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: $40 (3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CNY Artist Initiative 2027 · Everson Museum of Art
item.description: Competitive program at the Everson Museum of Art in Syracuse, New York: each year museum curators select regional artists for solo exhibitions in the Members' Council Gallery, running seven to nine weeks with accompanying programming such as artist talks and workshops. Open to artists living and working within a 75-mile radius of Syracuse. Selections are based on innovative quality, alignment with the museum's mission, and community relevance. 2027 exhibitions; apply with 20 images. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum solo exhibition.

item.title: Call for Exhibition Proposals · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Artlink Contemporary Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana, accepts proposals for solo, group, and curated exhibitions, reviewed once a year after March 1 by the Artlink Artist Panel and Exhibition Coordinator for the following year's schedule. Selected artists receive an exhibition contract and a flexible gallery space. Proposals are evaluated on concept, cohesiveness, innovation, craftsmanship, and accessibility. National artists welcome; shipping and travel are not covered. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: $25. Prize: Gallery exhibition.

item.title: Cyanotype: A Celebration of Process and Possibility · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont celebrating cyanotype in any form — traditional contact prints, camera-made cyanotypes, photograms, digital negatives, toned and wet cyanotypes, mixed media and experimental approaches, as long as cyanotype is the primary component of the finished work. Juried by Sam Wang. Up to 35 images selected for the gallery exhibition and 40 more for the online gallery; all selected work appears in the exhibition catalog and remains on the gallery website. Exhibition September 4–26, 2026, closing with World Cyanotype Day workshops and artist talks on September 26. Prints due August 21. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $39 / 5 images + $6 each. Prize: $300 Juror's Award + Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Black & White Images — Photobook Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call from Treviso-based independent publisher Soft Publishing for black-and-white images of any subject — cohesive bodies of work or individual images. Up to 10 images per artist, minimum 2000px on one side, submitted with full captions (title, year, medium, dimensions) and a short description. Open to artists from anywhere and of all ages. Selected work is published in a limited-edition photobook. Free to enter via Google Form; selected artists are contacted by email. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 26th Annual Vivian & Stanley Reed Marine Show · Stamford Art Association
item.description: Multimedia juried exhibit from the Stamford Art Association on all things marine — the sea, the seashore, boats, activity on or near the water. Up to 9 works in any medium, from artists across disciplines and experience levels; up to $400 in awards given for excellence and conformity to the theme, with a 30% commission on sales. Entry is $35 for the first piece and $15 for each additional (members $30/$10). Named for Vivian and Stanley Reed, two founding SAA members and avid sailors. Hand delivery only (receiving July 10–11). Exhibition online and at the Townhouse Gallery July 16 – August 20, 2026, with opening reception July 16. — Deadline: June 26, 2026. Fee: $35 + $15 each addl ($30/$10 members). Prize: Up to $400 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Light/Shadow · Fig Tree Gallery
item.description: All-media juried exhibition at Fig Tree Gallery, the long-running artists' co-op in downtown Fresno, exploring the broad concept of light and its counterpart. 2–5 images of 2D or 3D work; photographic and digital work accepted printed on permanent media such as paper or canvas. Open to California artists 18+ who are not gallery members; work must be original, for sale, and made within the last three years. Exhibition September 3–27, 2026 with opening during Fresno's September 3 Art Hop; in-person delivery August 21–23. Juried by a five-artist panel; 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $45 + $5 media fee. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Vehicles & Voyages · Arts Center East
item.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut celebrating the many ways we move through the world — cars, trucks, bicycles, motorcycles, boats, trains, aircraft, and the journeys they make possible. Historic vehicles, scenes of travel, personal road trips, maritime exploration, or imagined voyages into the future: movement, connection, freedom, and discovery. All media and artistic styles welcome, including photography; open to artists 18+. Entry $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), $5 each additional piece up to five. Shown August 8 – September 12, 2026, with reception and awards August 22. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: $35–$55. Prize: Exhibition.
